text:
eli: Quick follow-up from the prefix-KV RFC — hitting a correctness edge-case when we share prefix entries across tenants. Repro: two tenants A/B that reuse same model shard; tenant A evicts a prefix and writes back a compressed KV that still gets served to B, causing garbled past-kv reads. Seen in prod 3x over the last week.

maya: ugh. Can you paste the smallest repro logs?

eli: sure — minimal tail of the log:
``` 
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z [runtime] tenant=A load_prefix key=enc-0x9f3 size=2.1MB
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z [runtime] evict prefix enc-0x9f3 -> compressed: true
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z [runtime] tenant=B load_prefix key=enc-0x9f3 served_from=shared_pool
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z [decoder] decomposition error: wrong-shape (kv_len mismatch)
```

eli: TL;DR: shared pool returned an entry that wasn't properly isolated per-tenant (shape/schema incompatible after quantization/packing).

pranav: is the key encoding including tenant id? if not, we should namespace keys by tenant or model version. cheap fix but increases memory.

sasha: namespacing fixes correctness but kills sharing benefits for identical workloads. Also increases cache fragmentation — worried about tail latency jumps when tenants are cold.

maya: what about a hybrid: keep a shared read-only prefix cache for immutable prefixes (from model blob + version) and tenant-scoped mutable tails? we already tag prefix entries with model_version in the loader, could expand that tag to include a canonicalization step.

eli: yep that was one idea. Another is to add a small header on cached blobs: {model_id, model_version, packing_format, tenant_affinity_flag}. Reject reads if header mismatches consumer. cheap-runtime check that avoids full deserialization.

pranav: +1 for header check. Also think we should add an LRU weight per tenant — weighted eviction so big noisy tenants can't evict small ones. we can combine with a short TTL for shared entries so they refresh after quantization changes.

sasha: weighted eviction is ok but complexity explodes: per-tenant LRU windows, cross-tenant accounting on GC. ops will love debugging that 😂. We should prototype a simpler path: 1) header validation, 2) conservative shared-pool policy (only share prefixes that are marked immutable at load time), 3) metrics to detect header rejections.

runtime-bot: cache-metrics: shared_pool_hit_rate=0.64, header_rejects=12 (last 24h), avg_evict_latency=4ms

eli: agreed to prototype sasha's conservative path first. If header_rejects stay >0.1% we escalate to per-tenant namespacing + weighted LRU.

maya: can we also add an enum for packing_format so future quant formats won't accidentally be mis-read? that would make header validation future-proof.

pranav: +enum. also we should add an integration test that replays mixed-tenant load with different packing formats and asserts no cross-tenant decode. add to eng-ci perf-nightly.

sasha: note: this doesn't fully solve correctness when we allow on-the-fly re-quantization (runtime adaptive quant). if we do that, we must either pin prefixes or version them with a strong id (content-hash) and refuse old formats.

eli: good call. for follow-ups:
- add header fields: {model_id, model_version, packing_format, tenant_scope_flag} (owner: eli)
- conservative shared-pool policy + rejection metrics (owner: sasha)
- enum for packing_format + CI test (owner: pranav)
- open an RFC addendum for long-term: tenant-weighted eviction and optional per-tenant namespaces (owner: maya)

maya: assigning items and will create the RFC addendum today. tagging @eng-sre for observability changes.

pranav: i'll add the CI test and a small perf microbenchmark to measure memory cost of namespacing.

sasha: i'll prototype header check and the shared-pool gating. i'll also add a debug flag to log header mismatches at INFO for 24h so we can estimate impact.

eli: thanks all. plan is to roll the header check as a safe server-side reject first (no behavioral change aside from metrics), then gradually enable conservative-sharing behind a flag. If metrics look good after two weeks we can consider reducing namespace separation. :thumbsup:

maya: sounds good. moving this to an RFC follow-up thread. :spiral_note_pad:
